title: Sheet Pan Sausage and Vegetables
metaDescription: Sheet pan sausage and vegetables roasted together on one tray — a hands-off 35-minute dinner with easy cleanup.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: sheet pan sausage, roasted vegetables, easy sheet pan dinner
ingredients: 1.5 lbs smoked sausage or kielbasa, sliced into rounds

steps.name: Preheat and start the potatoes
steps.text: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper, spread on a sheet pan, and roast for 10 minutes to give them a head start.

steps.name: Add the rest and roast
steps.text: Toss the sausage, bell peppers, onion and broccoli with remaining olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder and thyme. Add to the sheet pan with the potatoes and spread into a single layer.

steps.name: Finish roasting
steps.text: Roast for another 15-18 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the vegetables are tender and lightly browned and the sausage is heated through.

tips.question: Why give the potatoes a head start?
tips.answer: Potatoes take longer to roast through than the sausage or other vegetables — starting them first keeps everything finishing at roughly the same time instead of undercooked potatoes.

tips.question: Can I use a different sausage?
tips.answer: Yes — chicken sausage or Italian sausage links (sliced) both work, just adjust cook time slightly if using raw uncooked sausage rather than pre-smoked.

tips.question: How do I keep the vegetables from steaming instead of roasting?
tips.answer: Spread everything in a single layer with space between pieces — an overcrowded pan traps steam and the vegetables won't brown.

storyIntro: This is the dinner for nights when I don't want to stand at the stove. Everything roasts on one tray, so there's no juggling multiple pans or timing side dishes separately.
The smoked sausage does a lot of the flavor work, so the seasoning stays simple and the vegetables just need room on the pan to actually roast instead of steam.
storyNote: Give everything space on the pan — a crowded tray steams instead of roasts, and you lose the browned edges that make this dinner good.
